correctness.rationale: The proof independently establishes that initially white leaves disable their centers from rim-forcing, reduces the closure problem to degree-one B endpoints in components of a maximum-degree-two B-E graph, and proves both implications including isolated/cyclic boundaries. A five-state weighted transfer matrix has one state cycle for every permitted cyclic letter word except that each entirely alternating even word is falsely counted twice; the explicit correction removes exactly four copies of its weight. The determinant and logarithmic derivative yield the displayed rational series. Formal small-parameter scaling proves the parity-dependent minimum coefficient for all integers n>=3. The standalone Python standard-library checker at the included path performed exhaustive independent forcing simulations and two polynomial computations on 1,398,080 sets for n=3..10 and confirmed minimum formulas through n=40; those finite checks are not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: Comparison by implication with the original minimum-rank formulation, Row cutvertex/unicyclic minimum-number techniques, and the full-polynomial theory for cycles, wheels and threshold graphs shows no direct coverage of the stated all-set sunlet criterion or complete rational enumerator in the inspected material. The known value of the minimum forcing number is not claimed as new. Inaccessible Row full text, title aliases and potentially unpublished priority remain genuine risks, not proof of priority.

value.rationale: A natural standard graph invariant—the number of successful ordinary zero-forcing initial sets at every cardinality—is solved exactly for the infinite sunlet family, beyond an already-known minimum. The static alternating-component criterion is a useful recognition theorem, and the fixed rational generating function enables all coefficients by a cubic recurrence; the parity-separated number of minimum sets is a genuinely finer enumerative statistic. The unrestricted structural statement and complete cardinality distribution are more than a textbook restatement of a known minimum or isolated numerical cases.
